raw_text:
Thanks — here’s a 12-week, upper-body–focused progressive plan tailored for a 29‑year‑old recreational climber with right subacromial impingement (cleared for pain‑free range only, no overhead loading). The programme emphasizes shoulder-friendly strengthening, scapular control, rotator cuff, thoracic mobility, progressive loading below shoulder height, and eccentric/controlled work to build resilience while avoiding painful positions. It also includes general conditioning, lower-body maintenance, and recovery/nutrition guidance. Progress only while exercises remain pain‑free; if symptoms increase, stop the offending movement and return to the physio.

Structure overview
- Frequency: 3 gym sessions/week (Upper A, Lower/conditioning, Upper B), 1–2 optional climbing or skill sessions per week provided they are pain‑free and stay below troublesome ranges; 1 full rest day.
- Phases: Weeks 1–4 (Foundations: mobility, control, isometrics), Weeks 5–8 (Strength and capacity below 90°), Weeks 9–12 (Load progression, eccentric control, return-to‑climb prep). Each week has 3 planned gym sessions; sessions ~45–70 minutes.
- Intensity & progression: Increase load or reps every 1–2 weeks if exercises are pain‑free. Emphasize tempo, control, and full breathing. Avoid overhead presses or loading above shoulder height on the right arm.

Precautions & rules
- Pain rule: Work must be pain‑free through range. Mild ache is okay if it doesn’t increase during/after session; stop and consult physio if sharp pain, tingling, or lasting increased pain >24 hours.
- Avoid: Loaded overhead positions (e.g., standing barbell overhead press, heavy incline barbell work) on the right; heavy carrying or loading with shoulder elevated or shrugged.
- Focus on scapular upward rotation control, posterior capsule mobility, thoracic extension.
- Warm up before sessions and nerve/glide mobility if prescribed by physio.

Warm-up (before every session; 8–12 minutes)
1. Light cardio 4–6 minutes (bike/row at easy pace) to raise blood flow.
2. Thoracic mobility: seated/standing thoracic rotations 2 × 8 per side; foam roller T-spines 2 × 30–60s.
3. Scapular activation: banded pull-aparts (45° and horizontal) 2 × 12; wall slides or scapular slides (pain‑free) 2 × 10.
4. Rotator cuff warm-up: supine or prone external rotation with light band/dumbbell 2 × 15; prone Y’s with no weight or 1–2 kg 2 × 10 (pain‑free).

Phase 1 — Weeks 1–4: Foundations (stability, motor control, endurance)
Goal: re-establish rotator cuff/scapular control, posterior shoulder soft-tissue work, low-load strength endurance under 90° elevation.

Week 1–2 (3 sessions/week)
Session Upper A (Mon)
- Warm-up above.
- Scapular wall slides (pain-free) 3 × 10–12 slow.
- Isometric external rotation (elbow at side) — right and left: 4 × 10–12s holds at ~60% max.
- Banded row (seated or standing) 3 × 12–15, moderate band tension, focus scapula retraction.
- Incline/flat chest-supported dumbbell row (no trunk rotation) 3 × 10 each side, light-moderate weight.
- Side-lying external rotation (right & left) 3 × 12–15, light.
- Serratus punches on floor or bench (90° shoulder flexion but supported, pain‑free) 3 × 15.
- Light biceps/triceps (machine or cable) 2 × 12.
- Finish: thoracic mobility 2 × 8.

Session Lower / Conditioning (Wed)
- Warm-up.
- Goblet squat 4 × 8–12.
- Romanian deadlift (dumbbells) 3 × 8–10.
- Single-leg RDL or split squat 3 × 8 each side.
- Farmer carry (light–moderate) 3 × 30–45s — keep shoulder relaxed; avoid heavy loading if painful.
- Core: Pallof press (anti-rotation) 3 × 10 each side.
- Optional low-intensity cardio 10–15 minutes.

Session Upper B (Fri)
- Warm-up.
- Scapular retraction holds on TRX or rings 3 × 10–12s.
- Seated cable row (elbows close, scapula control) 3 × 10–12.
- Incline single-arm dumbbell bench press — limit elbow/arm path to below 90° elevation on right: 3 × 8–10 each side, left can be slightly heavier.
- Prone T/Y/I on bench 3 × 8–10 each.
- Banded external rotation at 45° abduction (door anchor) 3 × 12.
- Push-up progression on knees or incline (hands elevated) 3 × 8–12 — stop if any shoulder pain.
- Finish: stretch posterior cuff/pec doorway 2 × 30s.

Week 3–4 (progress slightly)
- Increase sets or reps: move rows to 3–4 × 10–15; increase isometric hold to 5 × 12s.
- Add single-arm cable face pulls (low to mid pull, emphasize external rotation) 3 × 12.
- Introduce eccentric-focused KB/wall slides: 3 × 8 slow (3–4s lowering phase).
- Farmer carries: increase time or weight carefully.

Phase 2 — Weeks 5–8: Strength & capacity (below shoulder height)
Goal: build strength of scapular retractors, rotator cuff, lats and mid/upper back, and increase load tolerance below 90°. Maintain pain-free rule.

Week 5–6
Session Upper A (Mon)
- Warm-up.
- Seated chest-supported row 4 × 8–10 heavier.
- Single-arm cable row with controlled eccentric 3 × 8–10 each, heavier on left as needed.
- Horizontal single-arm dumbbell press (bench at 0–15° decline to keep arm path low) 3 × 6–8 per side — avoid right overhead path.
- Lat pulldown to chest (stop where comfortable, aim under chin level, no pain) 3 × 8–10. If pulldown causes pain prefer chest-supported pullover machine or straight-arm pulldown 3 × 10–12.
- Prone external rotation with scapular retraction 3 × 12.
- Half-kneeling anti-rotation press (light) 3 × 8 each side.
- Rotator cuff band scaption to 60° (pain‑free) 3 × 12.

Session Lower / Conditioning (Wed)
- Warm-up.
- Deadlift variation (trap bar or hex bar) 3 × 5–6.
- Bulgarian split squat 3 × 8 each.
- Reverse lunge 3 × 8 each.
- Rower intervals 6 × 1 min work/1 min easy (moderate intensity).
- Core stability: dead bug 3 × 10.

Session Upper B (Fri)
- Warm-up.
- Single-arm landmine row or chest-supported single-arm row 4 × 8.
- Dumbbell bench press (flat) 3 × 6–8 (keep path low on right; avoid high finish).
- Single-arm low cable face pull / external rotation 3 × 10–12.
- Scaption with dumbbell 3 × 10 (to pain‑free height, usually < 90°).
- Incline plank with scapular protraction/retraction 3 × 30s.
- Rear delt fly (machine or cable) 3 × 12.

Week 7–8 (progress)
- Increase load on rows and horizontal presses 5–10% if pain-free.
- Add tempo: 3s eccentric on selected row and press sets (1–2 sets).
- Introduce slow negatives for external rotation: 3 × 8 with 3–4s eccentric for right arm.
- Add unilateral loaded carries (suitcase or rack) 3 × 30–45s — keep shoulder neutral.

Phase 3 — Weeks 9–12: Load progression, eccentric control, climb transfer
Goal: increase strength, improve eccentric tolerance and prepare for climbing movements while still avoiding painful ranges and overhead loading.

Week 9–10
Session Upper A (Mon)
- Warm-up.
- Heavy (relative) chest-supported single-arm row 4 × 6–8.
- Single-arm bench press or floor press 4 × 6 (floor press limits overhead).
- Bent-over single-arm dumbbell row 3 × 6–8 with slow eccentric.
- Cable straight-arm pulldown (lats) 3 × 10–12.
- Eccentric-focused external rotation (supine or cable) 3 × 6–8 with 4s lowering on right.
- Scapular pull-ups (band assisted) 3 × 6–8 (focus on scapular depression/retraction; partial ROM).

Session Lower / Conditioning (Wed)
- Continue lower strength maintenance: front squat or goblet 4 × 6–8.
- Hip hinge emphasis 3 × 6.
- Conditioning: 12–15 min intervals bike/row.
- Core: weighted carry + anti-rotation 3 rounds.

Session Upper B (Fri)
- Warm-up.
- Meadows/landmine single-arm row 4 × 8 (control).
- Floor press or dumbbell bench press (controlled) 4 × 6–8.
- High-rep scapular endurance work: band pull-aparts 3 × 20–25, serratus 3 × 20.
- Eccentric-loaded scapular push-downs (slow) 3 × 8.
- Rear delts/rotator cuff circuit: 3 rounds of 12 each.

Week 11–12 (integration & return prep)
- Emphasize heavier sets with low reps for main rows/presses if pain-free (4–6 reps).
- Continue eccentric loading for external rotation and scapular lowering.
- Add climbing-specific pulls: horizontal campus board holds or ring rows at various angles if pain‑free and under physio agreement — keep to pain‑free ROM and no full overhead lockouts on right.
- Gradually reintroduce above-shoulder movement only if cleared and pain-free for several consecutive sessions; otherwise continue below 90° work.

Sample progression week (Week 12 example)
Upper A
- Warm-up.
- Chest-supported single-arm row 5 × 5 heavy.
- Floor press 4 × 5.
- Straight-arm pulldown 3 × 10.
- Eccentric external rotation 3 × 6 (4s eccentric).
- Scapular pull-ups 3 × 6.
- Finish: thoracic extension & pec stretch.

Lower/conditioning
- Front squat 4 × 6.
- Deadlift or trap-bar 3 × 4–6.
- Intervals 10–12 mins.
- Core circuit.

Upper B
- Meadows row / heavy single-arm row 4 × 6.
- Single-arm floor press 3 × 6–8.
- Scapular endurance circuit 3 rounds.
- Rotator cuff/ posterior chain maintenance.

Accessory details (rotator cuff & scapula)
- Isometrics: external rotation and scaption holds early-phase and maintained throughout.
- Scapular endurance: band pull-aparts high reps and serratus punches.
- Posterior capsule: doorway stretches and sleeper stretch only if cleared by physio.
- Thoracic mobility: foam rolling and extension drills 3–5 times/week.

Return-to-climb guidance
- Only add climbing sessions when shoulder is pain-free through daily activities and gym sessions for at least 2–3 weeks.
- Start with easy traversing, low holds, high feet, avoid dynamic moves and overhead reaches on right.
- Limit climbing session duration initially (20–30 min) and avoid repeat high-angle overhangs.
- Progress intensity and overhead reaches slowly and within pain-free range.

Recovery, sleep, and nutrition notes
- Sleep: aim for 7–9 hours per night to support tissue repair.
- Protein: 1.4–2.0 g/kg/day (rough guideline) to support muscle repair — spread across meals.
- Calories: maintain slight calorie surplus (~+150–300 kcal) only if increasing muscle; otherwise maintenance.
- Hydration: keep consistent; peri-workout carb is helpful if sessions are intense.
- Anti-inflammatory meds/ice: use as advised by physio/MD. Gentle icing post‑session for soreness can help; avoid masking progressive pain.
- Active recovery: gentle mobility, walking, foam rolling and sleep. Avoid aggressive stretching of irritated tissues.

Monitoring & progression cues
- Increase weight when target rep range is met for 2 consecutive sessions without pain.
- If pain increases during or after training beyond baseline, reduce load, revert to previous phase, and consult physio.
- Track symptoms (location, intensity, timing) and functional goals (specific climb moves).

Equipment choices & substitutions
- Use chest-supported machines and benches to unload scapula as needed.
- Landmine or single-arm cable/DB alternatives for rows and presses.
- Bands for rotator cuff progression and scapular control.
- Trap-bar deadlifts and floor presses to avoid overhead strain.

Final notes
- Communicate with the client’s physio about the plan and get sign-off on any reintroduction of overhead movements.
- Emphasize patience — tendinous/impingement issues respond to consistent, progressive, pain‑free loading over weeks.
- If you want, I can convert this into printable week-by-week sheets, daily checklists, or a 12-week PDF with exercise photos and alternative exercises for any specific equipment constraints.
